description.body: When querying collections or EF Core results, understand the semantic difference between FirstOrDefault and SingleOrDefault. Use FirstOrDefault when multiple results may exist and you only need the first; use SingleOrDefault when exactly one or zero results are expected — SingleOrDefault throws if multiple matches exist.

IEnumerable executes queries in-memory and is suitable for in-process collections. IQueryable enables expression tree translation and deferred execution on the data store (e.g., SQL via EF Core). Prefer IQueryable for large datasets and when composing server-side filters.

Use middleware to catch unhandled exceptions and return consistent problem details responses. Implement logging and map known exceptions to specific HTTP status codes to improve client feedback and observability.
Repository, Unit of Work, Dependency Injection, and Strategy patterns help keep Web API projects modular and testable. Use DI (built-in in ASP.NET Core) to manage lifetimes and keep controllers thin.
